issues.issue: Several AE rates in the text are not supported by the citation quotes: nausea 12.4% is not in the quote (quote shows '5.312.421.1' which supports 5.3 and 21.1 but 12.4 placement implies 0.75 mg column; still, 12.4 appears) and more importantly 'abdominal pain, and decreased appetite' values are not quantified; the placebo value for nausea (5.3) and diarrhea rates differ, and the mapping of numbers to doses cannot be verified from the stitched/merged OCR quote 'Nausea5.312.421.1'.

Uncited number: vomiting placebo 2.3%, 6.0% (0.75 mg), 12.7% (1.5 mg) appear in the quote 'Vomitingb2.36.012.7' so they are supported, but nausea 12.4% and 21.1% vs 5.3% are drawn from a run-together OCR string whose column-to-dose assignment is not explicit; flagged uncited numbers (12.4, 21.1, 5.3) should be verified before release.

Uncited-number flags for 0.75 and 1.5 are false positives — these are doses (dulaglutide 0.75 mg / 1.5 mg), which are excluded from scrutiny; the efficacy values and CIs are all supported by the citations.
Uncited-number flags for 0.75 and 1.5 are false positives — these are doses, not efficacy numbers; the HbA1c differences and CIs are supported by the citation.
Uncited-number flag for '2' is a false positive — it is part of 'type 2 diabetes', not an efficacy/safety statistic.
Uncited-number flag for '2' is a false positive — it refers to 'MEN 2', a condition name, not a statistic.
Uncited-number flag for '2' is a false positive — it is part of 'type 2 diabetes', not a statistic.

The primary receipt_date text 'September 18, 2014' is misleading/likely wrong as the application receipt date; the original BLA was submitted September 18, 2013, and September 18, 2014 is the PDUFA goal date — labeling 2014 as the receipt date confuses an administrative resubmission acknowledgement with the original receipt.
Priority_review present=false is plausible but not citation-verified; no evidence either way in provided quotes, so acceptable as default.

The endpoint 'Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26' is supported only by a table-fragment quote ('...52 weeks\tweek 26...') rather than an explicit endpoint statement; the citation does not clearly state HbA1c change as the primary endpoint for GBDC.
